# Results — Study 401 (Signal-Stacking)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The viral pitch: take **K weak
signals** — "none significant alone, most hovering around 52%" — normalise them into one
composite z-score "weighted by historical Sharpe," and the combination "produces something
retail has never seen." We build that machine and test it against its own controls. The honest
answer has a real kernel and a fatal catch: stacking **does** raise the information coefficient,
but only like **√K**, and **only when the signals carry genuine, decorrelated edge**. On a
pure-noise stack the composite times nothing; redundant signals plateau; and the gorgeous
"ζ-field vs buy-and-hold" curve is manufactured by **in-sample selection** that evaporates out
of sample. This is a **methods demo** (sibling of [343–350](../../343-data-mining-roulette/) and
[399](../../399-kalshi-efficiency/)); the real SPY tape is illustrative — no `REAL` stamp is
claimed. Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Synthetic core | deterministic analytic panel (`data.synthetic_panel`, seed 401); every IC & cross-correlation known in closed form |
| Real tape | yfinance daily SPY total-return closes → 12 textbook weak timing signals (`data.load_real`, cache-first) |
| Real window | 1995-10-16 → 2026-06-18 (**7,719** trading days; **30.7** years; **12** signals) |
| Real fingerprint | `a4bfd3d8a8cd` (`data.fingerprint`) |
| As-of | 2026-06-23 (cache built deterministically; no future stamp) |
| Two knobs | `signal_ic` (0 = pure-noise null; 0.05 = a real ~52% edge) · `signal_corr` (0 = decorrelated → √K; 0.9 = redundant → ceiling) |
| Honest arbiter | composite IC vs mean-single (the √K test), permutation p of the composite Sharpe, in/out-of-sample snoop split |

> **Methods-demo caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The lesson is the *mathematics of
> combination*, established on a controlled synthetic panel where the truth is known. The real
> SPY stack is an honest illustration of the machinery on a tape that is *not* a clean null — it
> can never back a `REAL` Signal stamp (that bar needs a robust *t* ≥ 2 on a real tradable edge,
> and stacking textbook timing signals on SPY produces the opposite). The verdict is a
> **methodology** verdict, in the spirit of the research-method demos.

## The null — stack ten coin-flips, manufacture nothing real

Ten pure-noise signals (`signal_ic = 0`, decorrelated). By construction nothing predicts the
return — individually *or* in any combination — so the composite can only bottle luck.

| metric | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| composite Sharpe (equal-weight) | **+0.11** (HAC *t* = 0.36) | indistinguishable from zero |
| best single / mean single Sharpe | +0.63 / +0.14 | the "best" of ten coin-flips looks fine by luck |
| composite IC | +0.0122 | ≈ the mean single IC (0.0147) |
| IC lift (composite ÷ mean single) | **0.83** | **no √K boost** (√K reference = 3.16) |
| permutation *p* | **0.375** | the composite Sharpe is squarely **inside** its own reshuffled null |

The composite of pure noise has **no** IC lift (0.83, not √10) and a permutation *p* of **0.38**:
reshuffling the signals into noise reproduces the "edge" more than a third of the time. Stacking
coin-flips manufactures nothing.

## The positive control — a real, decorrelated edge, and the √K boost appears

Ten weak signals each with a *planted* information coefficient of **0.05** (a ~52% hit-rate),
**decorrelated** (`signal_corr = 0`). Now the stacker has something genuine to compound.

| metric | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| composite Sharpe (equal-weight) | **+2.00** (HAC *t* = 6.40) | a real blend the harness banks |
| best single / mean single Sharpe | +1.21 / +0.71 | the composite beats the **best** single, not just the mean |
| composite IC | +0.1644 | well above the mean single IC (0.0535) |
| IC lift (composite ÷ mean single) | **3.07** | tracks the **√K reference of 3.16** — the legitimate kernel |
| permutation *p* | **0.000** | far outside the reshuffled null — a genuine link |

This is the honest half of the pitch: **decorrelated** weak edges add up like √K, the composite
beats the best single signal, and the permutation test fires. The catch is everything the pitch
omits — *real* and *decorrelated*.

## Redundancy kills it — fifty copies of one idea are worth barely more than one

Same planted edge (`signal_ic = 0.05`) but the signals are now **redundant** (`signal_corr =
0.9`): they mostly repeat each other.

| metric | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| composite Sharpe (equal-weight) | **+0.52** (HAC *t* = 1.67) | a quarter of the decorrelated blend |
| composite IC / mean single IC | +0.0524 / 0.0500 | barely moved |
| IC lift | **1.05** | **stuck near 1** (√K reference = 3.16) — the √K boost collapses |
| permutation *p* | 0.051 | the faint single-signal edge survives; **stacking added nothing** |

The √K law is really a √(*effective breadth*) law, and correlation is what destroys breadth. With
`corr = 0.9` ten signals are worth ≈ one: lift **1.05**, not 3.16. The knob the viral thread
never mentions is the one that decides everything.

## The √K curve — the whole ballgame in one table

Composite IC and its lift over the mean single signal, as the stack grows from K = 1 to 40. The
decorrelated case rides the √K line; the redundant case flatlines.

| K | decorrelated lift | redundant lift | √K reference |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 |
| 2 | 1.39 | 1.03 | 1.41 |
| 5 | 2.21 | 1.04 | 2.24 |
| 10 | 3.07 | 1.05 | 3.16 |
| 20 | 4.35 | 1.05 | 4.47 |
| 40 | **5.97** | **1.05** | 6.32 |

Decorrelated weak edges compound almost exactly like √K (5.97 vs 6.32 at K = 40). Redundant ones
hit a **ceiling of ~1.05** and stay there forever. Stacking is only as powerful as the signals
are *different*.

## The real tape — the same stack on SPY produces a negative composite

The identical 12-signal stack (momentum, MA-gaps, an oscillator, a low-vol screen, three pure
decoys) on SPY total-return, 1995→2026.

| metric | value | reading |
|---|--:|---|
| composite Sharpe (equal-weight) | **−0.26** (HAC *t* = −1.63) | the blend *loses* |
| best single / mean single Sharpe | +0.20 / −0.14 | no single signal carries a sign-timing edge |
| composite IC / mean single IC | −0.0666 / 0.0360 | the composite's sign is wrong |
| permutation *p* | **0.982** | the composite is worse than ~98% of reshuffled worlds |
| buy-and-hold Sharpe (excess) | +0.62 | simply holding SPY beats every blend |

On a real tape with no decorrelated edge to compound, stacking textbook timing signals produces a
**negative** composite (Sharpe −0.26, perm *p* = 0.98) that is comprehensively beaten by buy-and-
hold (+0.62). The machine works; there is just nothing for it to combine.

## The snooping tax — the gorgeous equity curve is in-sample selection

The p-hacker's move: rank single-signal Sharpes on the **first half**, keep the winners, weight
them by that in-sample Sharpe (the "weighted by historical Sharpe" recipe), and measure on the
**held-out half**. The gap is the snooping tax the headline curve hides.

| tape | IS Sharpe | OOS Sharpe | gap | chosen |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| positive control (real ic = 0.05) | +2.12 | +1.75 | +0.38 | 10 signals |
| null (pure noise) | +0.48 | +0.36 | +0.12 | 6 signals |
| **real SPY tape** | −0.05 | **−0.46** | +0.41 | `noise_a, ma_gap_200, noise_c, mom_60` |

When a real decorrelated edge exists, the snooped blend mostly **survives** out of sample (2.12 →
1.75). When it does not, the in-sample "edge" is selection noise: on SPY the snooper hand-picks
**two of the three pure decoys** (`noise_a`, `noise_c`) as "best signals," prints a flat IS
Sharpe, and then loses out of sample (−0.46). The headline ζ-field curve is built on exactly this
selection.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** This is a **methods demo**: the lesson (stacking lifts IC only ~√K, only for
  real decorrelated edges) is established on a controlled synthetic panel, and the real SPY stack
  is an honest illustration that *cannot* back a `REAL` stamp — the equal-weight composite on SPY
  is **negative** (Sharpe −0.26, permutation *p* = 0.98), comprehensively beaten by buy-and-hold.
  No real, harvestable stacking edge is claimed.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** On pure noise the composite Sharpe sits in its permutation null
  (*p* = 0.38, IC lift 0.83 — no √K); with redundant signals the lift plateaus at **1.05**; on
  SPY the blend loses to buy-and-hold. The only positive backtest is the **snooped** one, and its
  in-sample Sharpe **evaporates out of sample** (the SPY snooper even picks two pure decoys). EV
  comes from genuine decorrelated information, which the viral stack does not supply.
- **A composite edge? — BUSTED.** The "empire of weak signals" is √(*effective breadth*) wearing
  Greek letters. Stacking compounds an edge **only** when the signals are both *real* and
  *different* (the positive control: lift 3.07 ≈ √10, perm *p* = 0.000). Absent that — noise, or
  redundancy, or a real tape with no decorrelated edge — the "composite field" is luck plus
  in-sample selection. Same shape as the research-method demos [343–350](../../343-data-mining-roulette/)
  and [399](../../399-kalshi-efficiency/).
